back: A small text file sent by a web server and stored by the browser, then sent back so the site recognises the user.
Kept in temporary memory; deleted when the browser closes.
Saved on the device; lasts until its expiry date or until deleted.
Saving personal details; tracking preferences; holding items in a shopping basket; storing login details.
Set by a different domain (e.g. an advertiser) and used to track users across sites.

front: Can a cookie carry a virus?
back: No. It is a small text file of data and cannot run.
Browsing can be tracked and a profile built; on shared computers others may access accounts.
Delete them, block third-party cookies, use private browsing, decline non-essential cookies, log out.
